All 22 tools confirmed to have non-empty inputSchema.properties via schema-integrity.test.ts (24 tests, all pass). MUTUAL_EXCLUSIVITY_PATH_MSG thrown by resolveProjectPath when both project_path and cwd_path are provided — confirmed by test and source review. Build succeeds cleanly. No regressions detected.

comments.note: schema-integrity.test.ts (WP-003) serves as a live automated regression guard — each of the 22 tools gets its own named test, so any future Zod-wrapping regression will be caught immediately with a clear tool name in the failure output.

Edge case verified: project-lifecycle.ts:377 still uses .refine() on an internal string value (plan archive filename), not on a top-level tool schema — this does not cause ZodEffects wrapping on the inputSchema, and schema-integrity confirms that tool's properties are non-empty.

resolveProjectPath correctly handles all 4 input states: project_path only (validate + return), cwd_path only (detect), both (throw MUTUAL_EXCLUSIVITY_PATH_MSG), neither (falls through to NOT_FOUND error). All paths covered by tests.

summary:
Code review PASS. WP-005 is a verification-only WP (no new code) that confirms all five ACs for the full four-WP refactor plan. Review covered all source changes across WP-001 through WP-004. No blocking issues found across any of the four work packages. The implementation is surgical, complete, and architecturally sound.

**WP-001 — `resolveProjectPath()` mutual exclusivity guard:** Guard placed at the very top of the function, fails-fast before any other logic. Uses `MUTUAL_EXCLUSIVITY_PATH_MSG` constant for message consistency. The truthy evaluation (`args.project_path && args.cwd_path`) is exactly consistent with the pre-existing `mutuallyExclusivePaths` predicate semantics. Inline comment with bug report reference provides clear historical context. Empty-string short-circuit edge case is intentional, consistent, and explicitly tested. Integration test in workflow-next-action.test.ts correctly verifies both `isError:true` and message shape.

**WP-002 — `.refine()` removal across 7 tool files:** grep confirms zero schema-level `.refine()` calls remain in any tool file. The only `.refine()` in the tool layer is the preserved field-level one at project-lifecycle.ts:377 on `plan_file` inside `InitializeProjectSchema` — correct and untouched. All `mutuallyExclusivePaths` and `MUTUAL_EXCLUSIVITY_PATH_MSG` imports cleaned from all 7 tool files. `BeginWorkSchema` examined directly — clean `z.object()` with no `.refine()`, no unused imports.

**WP-003 — `schema-integrity.test.ts`:** Exemplary test file. Clear header with root-cause explanation and constraint cross-references (§63). Correct use of `beforeAll` for single-shot synchronous registration. Two-layer structural guard (count + per-name coverage) ensures a newly added tool without a corresponding test entry breaks immediately with a clear tool-name failure message. Mock `McpServer` intercept pattern exercises the exact production registration path without source changes. `zodToJsonSchema` assertion correctly distinguishes `ZodObject` (non-empty properties) from `ZodEffects` (empty properties).

**WP-004 — Constraint documentation:** §63 is complete and authoritative: Rule, Reason, Correct Pattern (code block), Anti-pattern (code block), Exception for field-level `.refine()`, Regression guard reference to `schema-integrity.test.ts`, and Background context. §64 codifies the mock `McpServer` testing pattern, converting a Developer Gold Nugget into permanently available guidance. §57 forward-reference to §63 added for discoverability. All formatting conventions followed precisely.

**Live verification:** 1038/1038 tests pass (34 files), `tsc --noEmit` exits 0.

comments.note: mutuallyExclusivePaths and MUTUAL_EXCLUSIVITY_PATH_MSG in path-validator.ts are now dead code outside test files — no production tool file imports them. Adding @deprecated JSDoc tags to both exports would cost nothing and make their transitional status explicit to future contributors without breaking backward-compatible usage.

zod-to-json-schema is imported directly in schema-integrity.test.ts but declared only as a transitive dep of @modelcontextprotocol/sdk. If the SDK drops it in a future release, the test suite breaks at import with a non-obvious error. Recommend adding an explicit devDependency entry (e.g., `"zod-to-json-schema": "*"` or pinned to the current resolved version) in mcp-server/package.json. Three independent agents (Developer, QA, Reviewer) flagged this consistently — low risk but clear right action.

Gold Nugget (codified by Documentation in §64): The mock McpServer intercept pattern in schema-integrity.test.ts is reusable for any future test inspecting tool metadata (descriptions, parameter constraints, enumeration values) without a real server lifecycle. §64 in constraints.md preserves this pattern with a full code example and usage guidance.
